Heard Sri Srininvas Velagapudi, learned counsel for the petitioner/appellant, and Sri Pratusha Bopanna, learned counsel for respondents.
Perused the entire material available on record.

2. The present Second Appeal is filed by the appellant assailing the judgment and decree, dated 14.07.2011, passed by the III Additional District Judge (Fast Track Court), Ranga Reddy District in AS.No.11 of 2006, wherein and whereby the judgment and decree dated 24.11.2005 passed by the II Additional Senior Civil Judge, Ranga Reddy District at L.B.Nagar in OS.No.815 of 1997 was set aside.

sentences.text: As there is delay of 1951 days in preferring the Second Appeal, the appellant filed SAMP.No.609 of 2017 to condone the delay.
3. Without referring to the merits of the Second Appeal, it is appropriate to first consider the SAMP.No.609 of 2017 filed for condonation of delay of 1951 days in preferring the Second Appeal.
LNA, J In/and 4.

In the affidavit filed in support of the application, the petitioner/appellant inter alia averred that as he was engaged in connection with the marriage of his elder brother's son, he entrusted the matter to one Sri K.Raji Reddy, Advocate, for filing Second Appeal, but during the shifting of the office of the said advocate, the case bundle along with the certified copies of the judgments and decrees of the Courts below appears to have been misplaced by one of his juniors viz., Bala Krishna Reddy, Advocate, who left the office without informing about the said misplacement.

That recently,
when he approached the Advocate- K.Raji Reddy, he was informed that the latter has already addressed a letter to his old address at Torrur informing about the misplacement, however, as he shifted his residence to Hyderabad he has not received the same.
Later, on thorough search, the case bundle was traced and immediately, he entrusted the matter to the Advocate for filing the Second Appeal.

Thus, the delay that occurred in filing the Second Appeal is neither willful nor wanton and prays the Court to condone the delay.
5.

Learned counsel for the petitioner contended that the delay occurred due to the reasons stated in the affidavit filed by the LNA, J In/and petitioner and as such, the delay is neither willful nor wanton and as the cause shown for the delay is bonafide, the same needs to be condoned.
In support of his submission, learned counsel relied upon the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in Basawaraj and another v. Special Land Acquisition Officer 1.

sentences.text:
In Basawaraj's case (cited supra), the Hon'ble Apex Court held as under:
"11.

The expression "sufficient cause" should be given a liberal interpretation to ensure that substantial justice is done, but only so long as negligence, inaction or lack of bona fides cannot be imputed to the party concerned, whether or not sufficient cause has been furnished, can be decided on the facts of a particular case and no straitjacket formula is possible.
(Vide Madanlal Vs. Shyamlal {(2002) 1 SCC 535} and Ram Nath Sao v. Gobardhan Sao {(2002) 3 SCC 195}.

entities.text: Ram Nath Sao v. Gobardhan Sao {(2002) 3 SCC 195}
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 12. It is a settled legal proposition that law of limitation may harshly affect a particular party but it has to be applied with all its rigour when the statute so prescribes.
The court has no power to extend the period of limitation on equitable grounds.
"A result flowing from a statutory provision is never an evil.
A court has no power to ignore that provision to relieve what it considers a distress resulting from its operation."
The statutory provision may cause hardship or inconvenience to a particular party but the court has no choice but to enforce it giving full effect to the same.
The legal maxim dura lex sed lex which means "the law is hard but it is the law", stands attracted in such a situation.

It has consistently been held that,
"inconvenience is not" a decisive factor to be considered while interpreting a statute.
xxx 15.

The law on the issue can be summarised to the effect that where a case has been presented in the court beyond limitation, the applicant has to explain the court as to what was the "sufficient cause" which means an adequate and enough reason LNA, J In/and which prevented him to approach the court within limitation.

In case a party is found to be negligent, or for want of bona fide on his part in the facts and circumstances of the case, or found to have not acted diligently or remained inactive,
there cannot be a justified ground to condone the delay.
No court could be justified in condoning such an inordinate delay by imposing any condition whatsoever.
The application is to be decided only within the parameters laid down by this Court in regard to the condonation of delay.

In case there was no sufficient cause to prevent a litigant to approach the court on time condoning the delay without any justification,

sentences.text: From a reading of the aforesaid observations, it is clear that the Hon'ble Apex Court at paras-11 and 12 of the judgment interpreted the expression "sufficient cause" and at para-15 summarized the law with regard to the issue of limitation.

9. While applying the parameters laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court with regard to the condonation of delay to the instant case, it is to be held that the aforesaid judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court would not support the case of the petitioner and in fact, it is against to the petitioner.

Executive Engineer, Jalgaon Medium Project and another 7, it was held as under:-
"17. .........

sentences.text: The evidence on record suggests neglect of its own right for long time in preferring appeals.
The court cannot enquire into belated and stale claims on the ground of equity.
Delay defeats equity.
The court helps those who are vigilant and "do not slumber over their rights".

and observed that taking very lenient view in condoning the delay, particularly, on the part of the Government and Government Undertaking, would not be proper and held as under:-
"29.
It needs no restatement at our hands that the object for fixing time-limit for litigation is based on public policy fixing a lifespan for legal remedy for the purpose of general welfare.
They are meant to see that the parties do not resort to dilatory tactics but avail their legal remedies promptly.
Salmond in his Jurisprudence states that the laws come to the assistance of the vigilant and not of the sleepy.
30. Public interest undoubtedly is a paramount consideration in exercising the courts' discretion wherever conferred upon it by the relevant statutes.
Pursuing stale claims and multiplicity of proceedings in no (2012) 3 SCC 563 (2008) 17 SC 448 LNA, J In/and manner subserves public interest.
Prompt and timely payment of compensation to the landlosers facilitating their rehabilitation/resettlement is equally an integral part of public policy.

Public interest demands that the State or the beneficiary of acquisition, as the case may be, should not be allowed to indulge in any act to unsettle the settled legal rights accrued in law by resorting to avoidable litigation unless the claimants are guilty of deriving benefit to which they are otherwise not entitled, in any fraudulent manner.
One should not forget the basic fact that what is acquired is not the land but the livelihood of the landlosers.
These public interest parameters ought to be kept in mind by the courts while exercising the discretion dealing with the application filed under Section 5 of the Limitation Act.

Dragging the landlosers to courts of law years after the termination of legal proceedings would not serve any Malreddy Rami Reddy vs Smt. S. Venkatamma , Venkata Lakshmi on 7 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/146982448/

Settled rights cannot be lightly interfered with by condoning inordinate delay without there being any proper explanation of such delay on the ground of involvement of public revenue.
It serves no public interest."

11. In Government of Maharashtra (Water Resources Department) reptd. by Executive Engineer vs.
Borse Brothers Engineers and Contractors Private Limited 8, the Hon'ble Apex Court held as under:
"63. ...... In a fit case in which a party has otherwise acted bona fide and not in a negligent manner, a short delay beyond such period can, in the discretion of the court, be condoned, always (2021) 6 SCC 460 LNA, J In/and bearing in mind that the other side of the picture is that the opposite party may have acquired both in equity and justice, what may now be lost by the first party's inaction, negligence or laches."
12.

sentences.text: From the aforesaid judgments of the Hon'ble Apex Court, it is well settled that condonation of delay is not a matter of right and unless sufficient and plausible reasons are shown, the delay cannot be condoned.
While condoning the delay, the Courts should also see the substantial rights accrued to the opposite party and also the passage of considerable time.

13. In the present case, after disposal of the Appeal by the First Appellate Court, respondent No.2 has executed registered sale deed dated 07.12.2011 in favour of respondent No.1 in respect of the suit schedule property.
Thus, substantial rights have been accrued in favour of third parties.

14. Following the observation of the Hon'ble Apex Court in Borse Brothers Engineers and Contractors Private Limited's case (cited supra), wherein it is held that while condoning the delay,
the Courts should always bear in mind that the other side of the picture LNA, J In/and is that the opposite party may have acquired both in equity and justice, what may now be lost by the first party's inaction, negligence or laches.

sentences.text: In the present case, since the substantial rights have accrued to the third party, it is to be held that it is not a fit case to condone the inordinate delay of 1951 days in filing the Second Appeal.
15. The petitioner did not choose to file the affidavit of the junior Advocate who allegedly misplaced the case bundle to show bona fide on his part in pursuing the matter.

Further, the affidavit filed by one Sri K.Raji Reddy, Advocate, to whom the petitioner was said to have entrusted the case, also does not give the exact details as to when the matter was entrusted to him by the petitioner and when his office was shifted during which the case bundle was misplaced and when the bundle was traced.

16. That apart, even the petitioner in the affidavit except vaguely stating that he was engaged with connection to the marriage of his elder brother's son, did not state when the said marriage was performed and the date when he shifted his residence from Torrur to Hyderabad.

sentences.text:
Thus, from the above, it is clear that both in the affidavits of the petitioner and the Advocate,
except narrating the so-called events that transpired due to which delay occurred, the exact dates of those events were not given.
18.

Condonation of delay is not a matter of routine, more so when there is huge inordinate delay and, therefore, the petitioner ought to have offered detailed, cogent reasons, plausible explanation for such delay.
Therefore, this Court finds that there is clear negligence on part of the petitioner in pursuing the matter and not informing about his change of address to his Advocate.

19. The reasons stated in the affidavit are vague, unsatisfactory and does not inspire the confidence of this Court, more so, when there is inordinate delay of 1951 days i.e., more than five years in preferring the Second Appeal.

20. In view of the foregoing reasons and the legal position and as no plausible and convincing reasons are shown for condonation of inordinate delay of 1951 days, SAMP.No.609 of 2017 deserves LNA, J In/and to be dismissed and is accordingly dismissed.
Consequently, the Second Appeal also stands dismissed.
No costs.
21. Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed.
___ JUSTICE LAXMI NARAYANA ALISHETTY Date:07.06.2024
